title: A world kids can believe in.
intro: Summer camp, built around queer community. Kids come for the activities and friendships, and meet grown-ups who help them picture their own future.

heroMedia.alt: Campers laughing and enjoying activities at Camp Indigo Point.

campLife.heading: From breakfast to the last campfire song.
campLife.summary: Swim. Make something. Try archery. Sing too loudly. Read in a hammock. Indigo Point is a summer camp where LGBTQ+ kids get to spend their days being kids.

schedule.title: Start together.
schedule.description: Breakfast, time with your bunk, and the first activities of the day.

schedule.title: Try something new.
schedule.description: Activities with your bunk and choices that fit your interests, from the waterfront to the arts.

schedule.title: Take a breather.
schedule.description: Rest time for reading, writing, and recharging, with more activities to follow.

schedule.title: The whole camp gets in on it.
schedule.description: Campfires, capture the flag, silent discos, bunk nights, and camp traditions.

belonging.heading: Room to be yourself.
belonging.body: Names and pronouns are respected. Queer adults are part of everyday camp life. Kids can spend more time making friends and less time explaining themselves.
details: Cabins and yurts bring campers together with peers and counselors.
Bunk assignments take grade level and campers’ needs into account.
Private shower stalls and all-gender restrooms are available.
Talk with our team about accommodations and support before camp.

activities.heading: Full days. Your kind of fun.
activities.summary: Swim. Make something. Try archery. Sing too loudly. Read in a hammock. Indigo Point is a summer camp where LGBTQ+ kids get to spend their days being kids.
highlights: Arts and crafts, music, drama, and dance.
Archery, climbing, hiking, and camp games.
Campfires, bunk nights, and Queer Prom.

communityCare.heading: Care is part of camp.
communityCare.summary: Our community care team supports the mental, emotional, and social side of being away from home.
bullets: Counselors are part of campers’ daily lives.
Rest time and quieter spaces help campers recharge.
Discuss health needs and accommodations with our team before registering.

history.heading: Our story.
history.body: Indigo Point began with people who loved camp and wanted queer and trans kids to have a community of their own. Our first summer was in 2022. The idea was simple: give kids the fun of summer camp, and heroes and role models who are like them.
milestones: A community of 150 campers from 33 states.
Rooted in Jewish summer camping; open to all faiths and none.
